entities.summary: Papirius Fabianus was an Ancient Roman rhetorician and philosopher from the gens Papiria in the time of Tiberius and Caligula, in the first half of the 1st century AD. He was born in Rome, Italy, and died in 50 CE. Papirius Fabianus was known for his expertise in rhetorical theory and his writings on the topic of rhetoric. He was particularly influential in the development of the Roman rhetorical tradition, which would shape the way Romans thought about persuasion, argumentation, and public speaking. His works, including the treatise 'De Rhetorica', had a lasting impact on the education of Roman orators and statesmen. Papirius Fabianus's teachings also influenced the development of the Roman law, as his ideas on rhetoric and argumentation were incorporated into the Roman legal system. In the centuries following his death, Papirius Fabianus's works were widely studied and emulated by scholars and politicians across the Roman Empire. His legacy as a master rhetorician and philosopher has endured, with his ideas continuing to be studied and referenced in modern times.
